edges.description: The missense protein is degraded, lowering TBCE levels.
TBCE is the cofactor that holds alpha-tubulin for heterodimer assembly.
Loss of Golgi-localized TBCE fragments the Golgi apparatus of motor neurons in the pmn mouse.
Fewer assembled heterodimers are available to polymerize into microtubules.
Microtubule loss in long motor axons precedes their dying-back degeneration in the pmn mouse.
The discovery authors attribute the central neurodegeneration to the microtubule defect caused by hypomorphic TBCE; the neuronal steps in the brain have not been studied.
Disrupting the Golgi, or depleting TBCE, compromises the routing of tubulin from the Golgi into the axon.

edges.description: Restoring TBCE at the Golgi prevents the axonal degeneration in a dose-dependent manner.

edges.description: Weakness of the denervated ankle dorsiflexors.
Lower motor neuron involvement contributes to the infantile hypotonia.
Scoliosis is attributed to neuromuscular weakness; no source tests the mechanism.
Delay in the first year precedes overt regression; whether it reflects early degeneration or a developmental effect is not known.
The optic nerve is a central nervous system tract; no separate mechanism for the optic atrophy has been studied.
Iron deposits appear in older patients; how they relate to the neurodegeneration is not known.
TBCE protein level in patient cells.
Polymerized tubulin, microtubule regrowth and spindle structure in patient cells.
edges.limitations: Dividing dermal fibroblasts are not neurons; the effect of the same defect on long motor axons and central neurons is inferred.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous germline TBCE variants combining the recurrent missense allele p.Ile155Asn with itself or with a frameshift allele. The missense protein is unstable rather than absent, and the disease differs from the developmental Sanjad-Sakati syndrome caused by other TBCE alleles, which the discovery authors interpret as hypomorphic variants driving neurodegeneration.

nodes.description: Spontaneous mouse mutant homozygous for a Tbce missense allele at the last residue of the protein, which lowers TBCE stability. Motor axons degenerate from the endplate back to the cell body from two weeks of age, and the mice develop severe muscle weakness and respiratory failure and die at four to six weeks; a wild-type Tbce transgene restores a normal phenotype. The mice also have a sensory neuropathy and progressive hearing loss.

Patient fibroblasts carry less polymerized alpha-tubulin, regrow microtubules slowly after nocodazole depolymerization and form abnormal mitotic spindles, as tail fibroblasts of pmn mice do. In pmn mice, microtubules are lost from motor and sensory axons and polymerize poorly in dorsal root ganglion neurons.
